question: Should OpenClaw permanently support the three proposed plugin approval capabilities—external verifier registration, verifier completion, and bounded reusable-grant storage—with the stated deprecated-hook removal commitment?
rationale: The branch is a substantial public plugin API and persistent-state addition. The accepted RFC supports the broad direction, but only maintainers can commit to the long-term compatibility, deprecation, and operational contract.

options.title: Accept the narrow contract
options.body: Approve these three plugin capabilities, the Gateway-owned deny/final-ledger boundary, and the documented deprecation/removal commitment before a rebase and final merge review.

options.title: Narrow or defer the API
options.body: Require a smaller host seam or a revised RFC before adding reusable grants and durable attempt storage to the public plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow contract
recommendation.body: Approve these three plugin capabilities, the Gateway-owned deny/final-ledger boundary, and the documented deprecation/removal commitment before a rebase and final merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked design and reference-plugin implementation and are best positioned to clarify the intended contract, while the final acceptance remains with the repository's relevant code owners.
